1	---
2	id: 'user-management'
3	title: 'User Management'
4	subtitle: 'View, delete, and export user information.'
5	---
6	
7	You can view your users on the [Users page](/dashboard/project/_/auth/users) of the Dashboard. You can also view the contents of the Auth schema in the [Table Editor](/dashboard/project/_/editor).
8	
9	## Accessing user data via API
10	
11	For security, the Auth schema is not exposed in the auto-generated API. If you want to access users data via the API, you can create your own user tables in the `public` schema.
12	
13	Make sure to protect the table by enabling [Row Level Security](/docs/guides/database/postgres/row-level-security) and only granting the necessary privileges for each role. Reference the `auth.users` table to ensure data integrity. Specify `on delete cascade` in the reference. For example, a `public.profiles` table might look like this:
14	
15	```sql
16	create table public.profiles (
17	  id uuid not null references auth.users on delete cascade,
18	  first_name text,
19	  last_name text,
20	
21	  primary key (id)
22	);
23	
24	-- Grant the privileges the roles need
25	GRANT SELECT ON public.profiles TO anon;
26	GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON public.profiles TO authenticated;
27	GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON public.profiles TO service_role;
28	
29	-- Enable row level security for the table
30	alter table public.profiles enable row level security;
31	```
32	
33	<Admonition type="caution">
34	
35	Only use primary keys as [foreign key references](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/tutorial-fk.html) for schemas and tables like `auth.users` which are managed by Supabase. Postgres lets you specify a foreign key reference for columns backed by a unique index (not necessarily primary keys).
36	
37	Primary keys are **guaranteed not to change**. Columns, indices, constraints or other database objects managed by Supabase **may change at any time** and you should be careful when referencing them directly.
38	
39	</Admonition>
40	
41	To update your `public.profiles` table every time a user signs up, set up a trigger. If the trigger fails, it could block signups, so test your code thoroughly.
42	
43	```sql
44	-- inserts a row into public.profiles
45	create function public.handle_new_user()
46	returns trigger
47	language plpgsql
48	security definer set search_path = ''
49	as $$
50	begin
51	  insert into public.profiles (id, first_name, last_name)
52	  values (new.id, new.raw_user_meta_data ->> 'first_name', new.raw_user_meta_data ->> 'last_name');
53	  return new;
54	end;
55	$$;
56	
57	-- trigger the function every time a user is created
58	create trigger on_auth_user_created
59	  after insert on auth.users
60	  for each row execute procedure public.handle_new_user();
61	```
62	
63	## Adding and retrieving user metadata
64	
65	You can assign metadata to users on sign up:
66	
67	<Tabs
68	  scrollable
69	  size="small"
70	  type="underlined"
71	  defaultActiveId="js"
72	  queryGroup="language"
73	>
74	<TabPanel id="js" label="JavaScript">
75	
76	```js
77	import { createClient } from '@supabase/supabase-js'
78	const supabase = createClient(process.env.SUPABASE_URL!, process.env.SUPABASE_KEY!)
79	
80	// ---cut---
81	const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.signUp({
82	  email: 'valid.email@supabase.io',
83	  password: 'example-password',
84	  options: {
85	    data: {
86	      first_name: 'John',
87	      age: 27,
88	    },
89	  },
90	})
91	```
92	
93	</TabPanel>
94	<$Show if="sdk:dart">
95	<TabPanel id="dart" label="Dart">
96	
97	```dart
98	final res = await supabase.auth.signUp(
99	  email: 'valid.email@supabase.io',
100	  password: 'example-password',
101	  data: {
102	    'first_name': 'John',
103	    'age': 27,
104	  },
105	);
106	```
107	
108	</TabPanel>
109	</$Show>
110	<$Show if="sdk:swift">
111	<TabPanel id="swift" label="Swift">
112	
113	```swift
114	try await supabase.auth.signUp(
115	  email: "valid.email@supabase.io",
116	  password: "example-password",
117	  data: [
118	    "first_name": .string("John"),
119	    "age": .integer(27),
120	  ]
121	)
122	```
123	
124	</TabPanel>
125	</$Show>
126	<$Show if="sdk:kotlin">
127	<TabPanel id="kotlin" label="Kotlin">
128	
129	```kotlin
130	val data = supabase.auth.signUpWith(Email) {
131	    email = "valid.email@supabase.io"
132	    password = "example-password"
133	    data = buildJsonObject {
134	        put("first_name", "John")
135	        put("age", 27)
136	    }
137	}
138	```
139	
140	</TabPanel>
141	</$Show>
142	<$Show if="sdk:csharp">
143	<TabPanel id="csharp" label="C#">
144	
145	```c#
146	var session = await supabase.Auth.SignUp("valid.email@supabase.io", "example-password", new SignUpOptions
147	{
148	    Data = new Dictionary<string, object>
149	    {
150	        { "first_name", "John" },
151	        { "age", 27 }
152	    }
153	});
154	```
155	
156	</TabPanel>
157	</$Show>
158	</Tabs>
159	
160	User metadata is stored on the `raw_user_meta_data` column of the `auth.users` table. To view the metadata:
161	
162	<Tabs
163	  scrollable
164	  size="small"
165	  type="underlined"
166	  defaultActiveId="js"
167	  queryGroup="language"
168	>
169	<TabPanel id="js" label="JavaScript">
170	
171	```js
172	import { createClient } from '@supabase/supabase-js'
173	const supabase = createClient(process.env.SUPABASE_URL!, process.env.SUPABASE_KEY!)
174	
175	// ---cut---
176	const {
177	  data: { user },
178	} = await supabase.auth.getUser()
179	let metadata = user?.user_metadata
180	```
181	
182	</TabPanel>
183	<$Show if="sdk:dart">
184	<TabPanel id="dart" label="Dart">
185	
186	```dart
187	final User? user = supabase.auth.currentUser;
188	final Map<String, dynamic>? metadata = user?.userMetadata;
189	```
190	
191	</TabPanel>
192	</$Show>
193	<$Show if="sdk:swift">
194	<TabPanel id="swift" label="Swift">
195	
196	```swift
197	let user = try await supabase.auth.user()
198	let metadata = user.userMetadata
199	```
200	
201	</TabPanel>
202	</$Show>
203	<$Show if="sdk:kotlin">
204	<TabPanel id="kotlin" label="Kotlin">
205	
206	```kotlin
207	val user = supabase.auth.retrieveUserForCurrentSession()
208	//Or you can use the user from the current session:
209	val user = supabase.auth.currentUserOrNull()
210	val metadata = user?.userMetadata
211	```
212	
213	</TabPanel>
214	</$Show>
215	<$Show if="sdk:csharp">
216	<TabPanel id="csharp" label="C#">
217	
218	```c#
219	var user = supabase.Auth.CurrentUser;
220	var metadata = user?.UserMetadata;
221	```
222	
223	</TabPanel>
224	</$Show>
225	</Tabs>
226	
227	## Deleting users
228	
229	You may delete users directly or via the management console at Authentication > Users. Note that deleting a user from the `auth.users` table does not automatically sign out a user. As Supabase makes use of JSON Web Tokens (JWT), a user's JWT will remain "valid" until it has expired.
230	
231	<Admonition type="caution">
232	
233	You cannot delete a user if they are the owner of any objects in Supabase Storage.
234	
235	You will encounter an error when you try to delete an Auth user that owns any Storage objects. If this happens, try deleting all the objects for that user, or reassign ownership to another user.
236	
237	</Admonition>
238	
239	### Removing account access
240	
241	When the goal is to remove an account so it can no longer access your app, delete the auth user with [`auth.admin.deleteUser()`](/docs/reference/javascript/auth-admin-deleteuser). With the default `shouldSoftDelete: false`, this removes the row from `auth.users`, which cascades to `auth.sessions` and invalidates the user's refresh tokens — so the account can no longer mint new access tokens.
242	
243	A few things are _not_ a substitute for deleting the user:
244	
245	- A temporary [ban](/docs/reference/javascript/auth-admin-updateuserbyid) only blocks sign-in for its duration and does not revoke existing sessions.
246	- Marking the account as deleted only in your own application tables leaves the `auth.users` row intact, so it can still authenticate and refresh.
247	
248	Deleting the user still cannot retroactively invalidate an access token that was already issued. Supabase access tokens are stateless JWTs, so a token already in the user's hands stays valid until its `exp` claim passes, and during that window the account can still call the API. You have two ways to handle this window:
249	
250	- **Bound it:** keep the [access token (JWT) expiry](/docs/guides/auth/sessions) short, so any outstanding token expires soon after you delete the user.
251	- **Close it for sensitive operations:** validate the `session_id` claim against the `auth.sessions` table on those operations. Because deleting the user removes the session row, an outstanding token fails this check — but only on the requests where you perform it; other API calls still accept the token until `exp`.
252	
253	See [User sessions](/docs/guides/auth/sessions) for details.
254	
255	## Exporting users
256	
257	As Supabase is built on top of Postgres, you can query the `auth.users` and `auth.identities` table via the `SQL Editor` tab to extract all users:
258	
259	```sql
260	select * from auth.users;
261	```
262	
263	You can then export the results as CSV.
264

---
id: 'user-management'
title: 'User Management'
subtitle: 'View, delete, and export user information.'
---

You can view your users on the [Users page](/dashboard/project/_/auth/users) of the Dashboard. You can also view the contents of the Auth schema in the [Table Editor](/dashboard/project/_/editor).

## Accessing user data via API

For security, the Auth schema is not exposed in the auto-generated API. If you want to access users data via the API, you can create your own user tables in the `public` schema.

Make sure to protect the table by enabling [Row Level Security](/docs/guides/database/postgres/row-level-security) and only granting the necessary privileges for each role. Reference the `auth.users` table to ensure data integrity. Specify `on delete cascade` in the reference. For example, a `public.profiles` table might look like this:

```sql
create table public.profiles (
  id uuid not null references auth.users on delete cascade,
  first_name text,
  last_name text,

  primary key (id)
);

-- Grant the privileges the roles need
GRANT SELECT ON public.profiles TO anon;
GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON public.profiles TO authenticated;
GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON public.profiles TO service_role;

-- Enable row level security for the table
alter table public.profiles enable row level security;
```

<Admonition type="caution">

Only use primary keys as [foreign key references](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/tutorial-fk.html) for schemas and tables like `auth.users` which are managed by Supabase. Postgres lets you specify a foreign key reference for columns backed by a unique index (not necessarily primary keys).

Primary keys are **guaranteed not to change**. Columns, indices, constraints or other database objects managed by Supabase **may change at any time** and you should be careful when referencing them directly.

</Admonition>

To update your `public.profiles` table every time a user signs up, set up a trigger. If the trigger fails, it could block signups, so test your code thoroughly.

```sql
-- inserts a row into public.profiles
create function public.handle_new_user()
returns trigger
language plpgsql
security definer set search_path = ''
as $$
begin
  insert into public.profiles (id, first_name, last_name)
  values (new.id, new.raw_user_meta_data ->> 'first_name', new.raw_user_meta_data ->> 'last_name');
  return new;
end;
$$;

-- trigger the function every time a user is created
create trigger on_auth_user_created
  after insert on auth.users
  for each row execute procedure public.handle_new_user();
```

## Adding and retrieving user metadata

You can assign metadata to users on sign up:

<Tabs
  scrollable
  size="small"
  type="underlined"
  defaultActiveId="js"
  queryGroup="language"
>
<TabPanel id="js" label="JavaScript">

```js
import { createClient } from '@supabase/supabase-js'
const supabase = createClient(process.env.SUPABASE_URL!, process.env.SUPABASE_KEY!)

// ---cut---
const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.signUp({
  email: 'valid.email@supabase.io',
  password: 'example-password',
  options: {
    data: {
      first_name: 'John',
      age: 27,
    },
  },
})
```

</TabPanel>
<$Show if="sdk:dart">
<TabPanel id="dart" label="Dart">

```dart
final res = await supabase.auth.signUp(
  email: 'valid.email@supabase.io',
  password: 'example-password',
  data: {
    'first_name': 'John',
    'age': 27,
  },
```

## Deleting users

You may delete users directly or via the management console at Authentication > Users. Note that deleting a user from the `auth.users` table does not automatically sign out a user. As Supabase makes use of JSON Web Tokens (JWT), a user's JWT will remain "valid" until it has expired.

<Admonition type="caution">

You cannot delete a user if they are the owner of any objects in Supabase Storage.

You will encounter an error when you try to delete an Auth user that owns any Storage objects. If this happens, try deleting all the objects for that user, or reassign ownership to another user.

</Admonition>

### Removing account access

When the goal is to remove an account so it can no longer access your app, delete the auth user with [`auth.admin.deleteUser()`](/docs/reference/javascript/auth-admin-deleteuser). With the default `shouldSoftDelete: false`, this removes the row from `auth.users`, which cascades to `auth.sessions` and invalidates the user's refresh tokens — so the account can no longer mint new access tokens.

A few things are _not_ a substitute for deleting the user:

- A temporary [ban](/docs/reference/javascript/auth-admin-updateuserbyid) only blocks sign-in for its duration and does not revoke existing sessions.
- Marking the account as deleted only in your own application tables leaves the `auth.users` row intact, so it can still authenticate and refresh.

Deleting the user still cannot retroactively invalidate an access token that was already issued. Supabase access tokens are stateless JWTs, so a token already in the user's hands stays valid until its `exp` claim passes, and during that window the account can still call the API. You have two ways to handle this window:

- **Bound it:** keep the [access token (JWT) expiry](/docs/guides/auth/sessions) short, so any outstanding token expires soon after you delete the user.
- **Close it for sensitive operations:** validate the `session_id` claim against the `auth.sessions` table on those operations. Because deleting the user removes the session row, an outstanding token fails this check — but only on the requests where you perform it; other API calls still accept the token until `exp`.

See [User sessions](/docs/guides/auth/sessions) for details.

## Exporting users

As Supabase is built on top of Postgres, you can query the `auth.users` and `auth.identities` table via the `SQL Editor` tab to extract all users:

```sql
select * from auth.users;
```

You can then export the results as CSV.
